how_merit_retention_works: Florida Supreme Court justices and district court of appeal judges are appointed by the governor from nominees submitted by a judicial nominating commission and then face voters in a yes-or-no 'merit retention' question ('Shall Justice/Judge ___ be retained in office?') at the first general election held more than one year after appointment and every six years thereafter. A simple majority of votes cast on the question retains the judge for a new six-year term; a majority 'no' vote creates a vacancy that the governor fills by appointment (Fla. Const. art. V, s. 10).
ballot_context: Every Florida ballot asks whether Supreme Court Justice Carlos G. Muñiz should be retained. Voters also answer a retention question for each District Court of Appeal judge standing in their district; which judges appear depends on the county (enter your address above to see yours). Names are verified against The Florida Bar's 2026 merit-retention list and county sample ballots. The Florida Bar discontinued its merit-retention poll in 2023, so there is no 2026 Bar poll.

judges.name: Carlos G. Muñiz
judges.ballot_question: Shall Justice Carlos G. Muñiz of the Supreme Court be retained in office?
judges.background: Born June 25, 1969, in Chicago. B.A. with high honors, University of Virginia (1991); J.D., Yale Law School (1997), where he was an editor of the Yale Law Journal. Law clerk to U.S. District Judge Thomas A. Flannery (D.C.) and Judge José A. Cabranes (U.S. Court of Appeals, 2nd Circuit). Deputy general counsel to Gov. Jeb Bush (2001), general counsel of the Department of Financial Services, deputy chief of staff and counsel to House Speaker Marco Rubio, deputy attorney general and chief of staff to Attorney General Pam Bondi (2011-2014), and general counsel of the U.S. Department of Education (2018-2019). Appointed to the Florida Supreme Court Jan. 22, 2019, as its 89th justice and the first Nicaraguan-American justice; retained by voters in 2020; served as the 57th Chief Justice of Florida from July 2022 to June 2026.

notable.item: Authored the court's April 1, 2024 majority opinion in Planned Parenthood of Southwest and Central Florida v. State, holding that the Florida Constitution's privacy clause does not protect abortion and upholding the state's 15-week abortion law (which allowed the six-week law to take effect).
Only Florida Supreme Court justice on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot; this is his second retention election (first retained in 2020).
Florida Channel produced an 'On the Ballot' profile segment on Justice Muñiz for the 2026 retention election.

judges.confirmation_status: On the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot (verified on The Florida Bar's 2026 merit-retention list and county sample ballots, including Sumter County's)
judges.background: B.A. in psychology and criminal justice, University of Oklahoma (1988); J.D., Florida State University College of Law (1991). Practiced business and commercial litigation in Brevard County for about 11 years. Appointed to the Brevard County Court by Gov. Jeb Bush in 2002 and to the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit (Brevard and Seminole counties) in 2006, where he served as an administrative judge and was twice elected chief judge (2013, 2017). Appointed to the Fifth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Rick Scott in July 2018 to succeed Judge Thomas D. Sawaya; retained by voters in 2020.

notable.item: Has served as Chief Judge of the Fifth District Court of Appeal.

judges.name: Scott D. Makar
judges.ballot_question: Shall Judge Scott Makar of the Fifth District Court of Appeal be retained in office?
judges.confirmation_status: On the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot (verified on The Florida Bar's 2026 merit-retention list and county sample ballots, including Sumter County's)
judges.appointed_by: Gov. Rick Scott (First DCA, 2012); recommissioned to the Fifth DCA by Gov. Ron DeSantis (2023)
judges.background: Born Oct. 15, 1959, in Mahopac, N.Y. B.S., Mercer University (1980); MBA and M.A. in economics (1982), J.D. with honors (1987) and Ph.D. in economics (1993), all from the University of Florida. Appellate attorney at Holland & Knight (1989-2001), chief of the appellate division of Jacksonville's Office of General Counsel (2001-2008) and Florida Solicitor General (2007-2012), arguing five cases before the U.S. Supreme Court. Appointed to the First District Court of Appeal by Gov. Rick Scott on Feb. 6, 2012, and recommissioned to the Fifth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Ron DeSantis on Jan. 1, 2023, when the appellate districts were redrawn. Has taught at several law schools.

notable.item: Argued cases for the state before the U.S. Supreme Court and Florida Supreme Court as Florida's Solicitor General before joining the appellate bench.

judges.background: B.A. in political science, Furman University (1989); J.D., Stetson University College of Law (1992). Assistant state attorney in the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit for two years, then in private practice in Orlando (Cameron, Marriott, Walsh, Hodges & Coleman; from 1996 Cabaniss, McDonald, Smith & Wiggins). Appointed to the Ninth Judicial Circuit (Orange and Osceola counties) by Gov. Charlie Crist in 2008 and to the Fifth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Rick Scott in 2013 to succeed Judge Bruce Jacobus.

notable.item: One of three Fifth DCA judges (with John M. Harris and Scott D. Makar) identified by Ballotpedia as standing for merit retention in November 2026.
